mainTopic: The size of the Sages' cubit (אביי vs. רבא), then רב's claim that שיעורין are a הלכה למשה מסיני
overview: This amud finishes the argument between אביי and רבא about whether every cubit the Sages mention is six handbreadths. A ברייתא says all cubits are six handbreadths but 'not exact', which fits רבא. אביי first rewords the ברייתא, and when that fails he says he follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The גמרא then shows that רבא needs no dispute between תנאים: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only adds that the כלאים cubit is not measured tightly. His words 'a cubit of six' exclude the altar's יסוד and סובב, and a פסוק in יחזקאל shows those used the small cubit of five. Next, the גמרא quotes רב: שיעורין, חציצין and מחיצין are a הלכה למשה מסיני. It challenges this with רב חנן, who says the פסוק 'ארץ חטה ושעורה' teaches measurements. It then explains the foods one by one: wheat, barley and vine. The answer to the challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רבא but challenges אביי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends 'provided they are not exact.' That works for רבא but seems to contradict אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...provided that they are not exact.' This works for רבא: some cubits are measured generously and others tightly. But for אביי it is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that says all cubits are six handbreadths but 'not exact.' It then says this fits רבא but is a problem for אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'not exact' means some six-handbreadth cubits are a bit bigger (שוחקות, for כלאים) and some a bit smaller (עצבות, for סוכה). Either way they are all six handbreadths, just as the ברייתא says. אביי does not hold that all cubits are six handbreadths, so a ברייתא saying 'all cubits' are six handbreadths contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: exact, precisely measured
granted, this works well for
'laughing': handbreadths measured generously, slightly spread
'sad': handbreadths measured tightly, slightly squeezed
it is a difficulty

steps.confusionAlert: The first words, 'שלא יהו מכוונות', are not a new statement. They are the last words of a ברייתא that began earlier.

phrases.english: provided that they are not exact.
phrases.notes: End of the ברייתא that began at the end of the previous amud (3b).

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava,
it means: so that these should be generous
phrases.notes: These are the cubits of כלאים.

phrases.english: and those should be tight.
phrases.notes: These are the cubits of סוכה and מבוי.

phrases.english: But according to Abaye, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אביי/רבא dispute from the previous amud by testing both views against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that not every cubit the Sages mention is six handbreadths
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'all cubits' are six handbreadths, only not exact. That matches רבא's generous/tight distinction and leaves no room for אביי.

steps.title: אביי rewords the ברייתא to speak only about כלאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the ברייתא as saying that only the cubit of כלאים is six handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could say to you: read it as 'The cubit of כלאים is measured with a cubit of six handbreadths.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by changing how we read the ברייתא. In his version, it only talks about the cubits of כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the six-handbreadth rule is limited to כלאים, it says nothing about סוכה or מבוי. Then אביי can still hold that those cubits are measured differently.

keyTerms.meaning: he could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
say / read it as (rewording a text)
forbidden mixtures, here plants sown together
a cubit of six handbreadths

phrases.english: Abaye could say to you: read it as:
The cubit of diverse kinds is measured with a cubit of six handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא puts all cubits in every area at six handbreadths.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only speaks about כלאים, so סוכה and מבוי can follow אביי's rule.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא shows the first part spoke about all cubits
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits his statement to כלאים, which implies the first תנא was talking about all cubits.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, all cubits the Sages mentioned regarding כלאים are six handbreadths, provided they are not exact. This implies that the first תנא was speaking about all cubits!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's rewording. It points to the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל specifically says 'cubits of כלאים.' That suggests he is disagreeing with the first תנא by narrowing the rule. So the first תנא must have been speaking about all cubits, which brings back the original difficulty for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter clause of a teaching
exact, precisely measured (same as מכוונות)
by inference, this implies
the first, anonymous תנא of the teaching

phrases.english: But since the latter clause teaches:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
All cubits that the Sages said regarding diverse kinds
are with a cubit of six handbreadths,
provided that they are not exact,
this implies that the first Tanna
is speaking about all cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the rewording offered in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rewording that limits the first part of the ברייתא to כלאים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא limits the rule to כלאים, so the רישא must have been broader and covered all cubits.

steps.title: אביי follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: אביי admits the first תנא disagrees with him and says he follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could say to you: Isn't there רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds like me? I am speaking in line with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי stops trying to reword the ברייתא. Instead he says he follows the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepts that the first תנא holds all cubits are six handbreadths. He points out that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the six-handbreadth cubit to כלאים, which supports his own view for סוכה and מבוי. An אמורא may follow one side of a dispute among תנאים, so the ברייתא no longer refutes him.

keyTerms.meaning: holds like me, agrees with me
I who said it / I stated it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא matches רבא (first תנא). אביי survives because his view matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who limits the six-handbreadth cubit to כלאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא defends an אמורא: when a source seems to refute him, he aligns himself with a תנא inside that same source.

phrases.english: Abaye could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו מִי אִיכָּא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Isn't there Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
who holds like me?

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: I stated my view in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: וְלָאו מִי אִיכָּא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּקָאֵי כְּווֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by siding with the תנא of the סיפא instead of rewording the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Following one side of a dispute among תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי must fit the whole ברייתא, including the first תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so the first תנא's view does not refute him.

steps.title: Does רבא also need a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's view clearly depends on a dispute between תנאים. It then asks whether רבא's view must depend on one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For אביי, this is certainly a dispute between תנאים. For רבא, must we say it is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up where אביי stands and then turns to ask about רבא. This sets up the next move: explaining the ברייתא so that it fits רבא without any dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, אביי admitted that he only follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and the first תנא disagrees with him. Now the question is whether רבא is also tied to just one side of that ברייתא, or whether both תנאים can agree with him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים (the sages of the משנה era)
Certainly
Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)

phrases.english: According to Abaye, it is certainly a dispute of tanna'im.
phrases.notes: Based on Step 4, where אביי sided with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: According to Rava, must we say it is a dispute of tanna'im?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled אביי's position, the גמרא turns to test רבא against the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבא's view also requires siding with only one of the תנאים in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only adds that the כלאים cubit should not be measured tightly
steps.stepSummary: רבא can say that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees that all cubits are six handbreadths. His only addition is that the cubit of כלאים should not be measured with squeezed handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could tell you: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל came to teach us this: one should not measure the cubit of כלאים tightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers on behalf of רבא. There is no dispute, because רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is only adding a small detail about כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that every cubit is six handbreadths. Sometimes those handbreadths are measured loosely and sometimes tightly. According to this reading, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not argue with the first תנא about cubit size. He only teaches that for כלאים one may not use the tight, squeezed measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense given on someone's behalf)
To teach us
Forbidden mixtures of seeds planted together
He should not measure tightly or exactly

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
came to teach us this:
The cubit of diverse kinds — one should not measure it tightly.
phrases.notes: That is, do not use squeezed handbreadths for כלאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5 by reading רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as adding a detail, not disagreeing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No dispute between תנאים is needed for רבא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only teaches that the כלאים cubit is not measured tightly.
steps.confusionAlert: Here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is NOT saying that other cubits are five handbreadths. According to רבא, all cubits are six. The only question is whether the handbreadths are measured loosely or tightly.

steps.title: Then why does he say 'a cubit of six'?
steps.stepSummary: If he only meant 'do not measure tightly,' he should have said just that. Saying 'a cubit of six' seems to exclude the cubits of סוכה and מבוי, as if those were five handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him simply say: 'The cubit of כלאים should not be measured tightly.' What does the phrase 'a cubit of six' come to exclude? Doesn't it exclude the cubit of a סוכה and the cubit of a מבוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading by pointing at the extra words רבן שמעון בן גמליאל used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his only point were 'don't measure tightly,' the words 'a cubit of six handbreadths' would be unnecessary. Extra words suggest that something is being excluded. The obvious candidates are סוכה and מבוי, which would then be five-handbreadth cubits. That would bring back a real dispute and go against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him say (the wording should have been simpler)
What does it come to exclude?
A cubit of six handbreadths
An alleyway, which needs a beam or post so one may carry in it

phrases.english: Then let him say: 'One should not measure the cubit of diverse kinds tightly.'
What does 'with a cubit of six' come to exclude?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו לְמַעוֹטֵי אַמַּת סוּכָּה וְאַמַּת מָבוֹי?
phrases.english: Is it not to exclude the cubit of a sukka and the cubit of an alleyway?
phrases.notes: This would imply that those cubits are only five handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 6 by pointing to words that answer does not explain.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as only adding 'do not measure tightly.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Extra wording must exclude something. The natural exclusion is סוכה and מבוי, which makes them five-handbreadth cubits and creates a dispute against רבא.

steps.title: 'Six' excludes the altar's base and ledge
steps.stepSummary: The words 'a cubit of six' do not exclude סוכה and מבוי. They exclude the cubits of the altar's יסוד and סובב, which everyone agrees are five handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to exclude the cubit of the יסוד and the cubit of the סובב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by finding a different thing that the extra words exclude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'six handbreadths' is not aimed at סוכה or מבוי. It is aimed at the special altar measurements, the יסוד and the סובב. Everyone agrees those are small, five-handbreadth cubits. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still agrees that all ordinary cubits are six, and רבא needs no dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The base of the altar, its bottom ledge
The ledge that goes around the altar higher up

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, both תנאים agree that all regular cubits are six handbreadths. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only adds that כלאים is not measured tightly. His words 'of six' exclude the altar's יסוד and סובב, which are five-handbreadth cubits for everyone.

phrases.english: No — it comes to exclude the cubit of the base
and the cubit of the surrounding ledge.
phrases.notes: Both are parts of the altar and are measured with five-handbreadth cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לְמַעוֹטֵי אַמָּה יְסוֹד וְאַמָּה סוֹבֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7 by pointing to a different exclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning what the extra wording excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A cubit of six' was thought to exclude סוכה and מבוי, implying they are five handbreadths.
steps.terutzMaskana: It excludes the altar's יסוד and סובב, which everyone agrees are five handbreadths. So רבא stands without a dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: The verse showing the altar's base and ledge used five-handbreadth cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in יחזקאל as the source that the יסוד and סובב of the altar were measured with a cubit of five handbreadths. It then explains each phrase of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'These are the measures of the altar in cubits — a cubit that is a cubit and a handbreadth. The bottom is a cubit, the breadth is a cubit, its border at its edge all around is a span, and this is the top of the altar.' 'The bottom of a cubit' is the יסוד. 'The breadth of a cubit' is the סובב. 'Its border at its edge all around' are the horns. 'This is the top of the altar' is the golden altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the source for what it just said in step 8: the altar's יסוד and סובב used a cubit of five handbreadths. It quotes a פסוק in יחזקאל and explains which part of the altar each phrase describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the general altar cubit is 'a cubit and a handbreadth', meaning a five-handbreadth cubit plus one more, which makes the normal six. But when it describes the יסוד and the סובב, it just says 'a cubit', with no added handbreadth. That shows those parts were measured with the smaller cubit of five, which is why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל had to say 'a cubit of six' to exclude them.

keyTerms.meaning: The base at the bottom of the outer altar
The ledge that runs around the middle of the altar
The 'horns', the raised corners of the altar
The golden altar inside the היכל, used for incense
'The bottom of a cubit', read here as the יסוד

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק shows that the altar's יסוד and סובב (and, in its explanation, the horns and the golden altar) were measured with the small cubit of five handbreadths. In step 8, the גמרא says 'a cubit of six' excludes the יסוד and סובב, not סוכה and מבוי. So according to רבא, the cubits of סוכה and מבוי stay at six.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And these are the measures of the altar in cubits
the cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth
phrases.notes: A five-handbreadth cubit plus one handbreadth, which equals the standard six.

phrases.english: and the bottom is a cubit, and the breadth is a cubit
phrases.notes: Here it says just 'a cubit', with no extra handbreadth, so it means a cubit of five.

phrases.aramaic: וּגְבוּלָהּ אֶל שְׂפָתָהּ סָבִיב זֶרֶת הָאֶחָד
phrases.english: and its border at its edge all around is one span
and this is the top of the altar.'
'The bottom of a cubit' — this is the base,
'and the breadth is a cubit' — this is the surrounding ledge,
'and its border at its edge all around' — these are the horns,
'and this is the top of the altar' — this is the golden altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the claim in step 8 that the יסוד and סובב cubits are five handbreadths.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the altar's יסוד and סובב were measured with five-handbreadth cubits
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל מג:יג, 'ואלה מדות המזבח באמות', with the explanation of each phrase

steps.title: רב: measurements, barriers, and partitions are a tradition from Sinai
steps.stepSummary: Since the topic is measurements, the גמרא quotes רב: שיעורין, חציצין and מחיצין are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: Measurements, barriers, and partitions are a law given to משה at Sinai.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It is linked to the previous one because both deal with measurements. רב teaches that three areas of halacha come from an oral tradition given to משה at Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה למשה מסיני is a law that has no source in a פסוק. It was passed down orally from Sinai. רב places three areas in this group: the sizes used in halacha (like a כזית), the rules of things that block immersion (חציצין), and the rules of partitions (מחיצין).

keyTerms.meaning: Halachic measurements, like a כזית or a כביצה
Barriers, things that block water from touching the body in a טבילה
Partitions, the halachic rules of walls and dividers
A law passed down orally from Sinai, without a פסוק as its source

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge. If שיעורין have a source in a פסוק, how can רב call them a tradition with no written source?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
Measurements, interpositions, and partitions
are a law given to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by topic only. The previous discussion was about the size of cubits, so the גמרא brings another teaching about measurements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שיעורין, חציצין and מחיצין are all a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Challenge: measurements seem to come from a פסוק in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב. Measurements seem to come from the תורה, since רב חנן says the פסוק 'ארץ חטה ושעורה' was said to teach measurements.
steps.simpleTranslation: Measurements?! They are from the תורה! As it is written: 'A land of wheat and barley…', and רב חנן said: This whole פסוק was said to teach measurements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first item on רב's list, שיעורין. It argues that measurements have a written source in the תורה, so they are not just a tradition from Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנן teaches that each food in the פסוק of the seven species hints at a different halachic measurement. If so, שיעורין are דאורייתא from a פסוק, which contradicts רב's claim that they are an oral tradition. The גמרא will now show this food by food.

keyTerms.meaning: From the written תורה
'A land of wheat and barley', the פסוק listing the seven species (דברים ח:ח)
Was said, meaning written in order to teach

steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect an answer yet. Here the גמרא only builds the challenge by explaining each food. The answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Measurements?! They are from the Torah!
As it is written: 'A land of wheat and barley, etc.'
And Rav Chanan said:
This entire verse was stated for measurements —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the first item in רב's statement in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that שיעורין are a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חנן says the פסוק of the seven species was said to teach measurements. So שיעורין have a written source in the תורה and are not only an oral tradition.

steps.title: Wheat teaches the time measure for a house with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how 'wheat' teaches a measurement. It quotes a משנה: clothes worn inside a בית המנוגע become impure only after the time it takes to eat half a loaf of wheat bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wheat' teaches what we learned in a משנה: If someone enters a house with צרעת carrying his clothes on his shoulders and his sandals and rings in his hands, he and they become impure right away. If he was wearing his clothes, his sandals were on his feet, and his rings were on his fingers, he becomes impure right away. But they stay pure until he stays long enough to eat half a loaf. That means wheat bread, not barley bread, eaten while reclining, with a side dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to back up the challenge by explaining the first food in the פסוק. Wheat is the source for the time measure in the laws of a בית המנוגע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Objects carried in his hands become impure the moment they enter, just like the person. Items he is wearing are 'protected' and become impure only after the time it takes to eat a פרס. That time is measured with wheat bread, which is eaten faster, and with a side dish, which makes eating faster still. So a halachic measurement is tied to wheat, which supports the claim that שיעורין come from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A house struck with צרעת
The time it takes to eat half a loaf (a פרס)
Reclining while eating
A side dish or relish eaten with bread

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate rules. The person always becomes impure right away. Only the items he is wearing get extra time. Items carried in his hands do not get that time.

phrases.english: 'Wheat' — for that which we learned in a mishnah:
One who enters a house afflicted with tzara'at
with his clothes on his shoulders,
and his sandals and rings in his hands —
he and they are impure immediately.
If he was wearing his clothes,
and his sandals were on his feet,
and his rings were on his fingers,
he is impure immediately,
but they remain pure until he stays
long enough to eat half a loaf —
wheat bread and not barley bread,
phrases.notes: This is the link to 'wheat' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: reclining and eating it with a relish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 11 by showing how the first food in the פסוק, wheat, teaches a halachic measurement.

steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נגעים about entering a בית המנוגע, where the time measure is based on eating a פרס of wheat bread

steps.title: Barley teaches the measurement for a bone of a dead person
steps.stepSummary: The word 'barley' in the פסוק is linked to a משנה: a bone from a מת the size of a barley grain makes things טמא through touching and carrying, but not through אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Barley': as we learned in a משנה: A bone the size of a barley grain makes things impure by touching and by carrying, but it does not make things impure through a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues showing how each word in the פסוק teaches a measurement. Now it explains the word 'barley' using a משנה about the bone of a dead person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as 'wheat' taught the half-loaf measurement in Step 12, 'barley' teaches the size of a barley grain. A bone of a מת that size causes טומאה when someone touches it or carries it. It does not cause טומאה to everything under the same roof (אהל). This is one more example backing up רב חנן's claim that measurements come from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A bone the size of a barley grain
Touching. One way a person or object becomes טמא
Carrying. Becoming טמא by lifting or moving the item, even without touching it
Being under the same roof as the source of טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: The bone does not lose its טומאה entirely. It still makes things טמא through מגע and משא. The only thing missing at this small size is טומאת אהל.

steps.title: Vine teaches the quarter-log of wine for a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The word 'vine' in the פסוק is linked to the measurement of a רביעית of wine, the amount that makes a נזיר liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Vine': the amount of a quarter-log of wine for a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through the פסוק. Now it explains that 'vine' teaches the amount of wine that a נזיר is punished for drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is forbidden to drink wine. The measurement that makes him liable is a רביעית. The גמרא connects this measurement to the word 'vine' in the פסוק, adding another example to רב חנן's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Vine. The third species in the פסוק
A quarter of a לוג. A standard liquid measurement
A person who took a vow to avoid wine and grape products, among other things
